title: Python for DSA
description: Learn Python with only what you need for Data Structures and Algorithms: from syntax to heaps, graphs and dynamic programming.

lessons.title: 01. Python Setup and First Program
lessons.notes:
Check your install: python3 --version
Run a file: python3 main.py
Indentation is part of the syntax (4 spaces).
Comments start with #.

lessons.title: 02. Variables, Types and Operators
lessons.notes:
int has no overflow. float is approximate.
// floor divide, % remainder, ** power, divmod(a, b)
Swap: a, b = b, a
None means 'no value'.

lessons.title: 03. Input, Output and Fast I/O
lessons.notes:
n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
Faster: import sys; input = sys.stdin.readline
Print many values once: print(' '.join(map(str, arr)))

lessons.title: 04. Conditionals and Loops
05. Functions and Scope
lessons.notes:
def, return (can return several values as a tuple)
*args, **kwargs, default values
lambda for tiny functions
nonlocal / global change outer variables.
Pitfall: never use def f(a=[]). Use None and create the list inside.

lessons.title: 06. Strings
lessons.notes:
Strings are immutable.
Slicing: s[::-1] reverses.
split, join, strip, ord, chr, f-strings.
Build text with a list and ''.join(parts). Repeated += is O(n^2).

logic.problem: Check if two words are anagrams.
logic.thinking: Same letters, same counts, any order.
logic.approach:
1. Count letters of both.
2. Compare the counts.
logic.code:
from collections import Counter
return Counter(a) == Counter(b)

lessons.title: 07. Lists as Arrays
lessons.notes:
append and pop() are O(1). insert(0, x) and pop(0) are O(n).
Slicing copies: arr[a:b] costs O(b-a).
2D grid: [[0]*n for _ in range(m)]. Never [[0]*n]*m.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

logic.problem: Find two numbers in a sorted list that add to a target.
logic.thinking: Brute force checks every pair. Sorting gives us direction.
logic.logic: Too small: move left up. Too big: move right down.
logic.approach:
1. l=0, r=n-1.
2. Compare sum with target.
3. Move one pointer.
logic.code:
l, r = 0, len(a) - 1
while l < r:
    s = a[l] + a[r]
    if s == t: return [l, r]
    l, r = (l + 1, r) if s < t else (l, r - 1)

lessons.title: 08. Tuples and Sets
lessons.notes:
Tuples are fixed and hashable (can be dict keys).
Sets hold unique items. Membership check is O(1) average.
| union, & intersection, - difference.

lessons.title: 09. Dictionaries and Hash Maps
lessons.notes:
d[key] = value, d.get(key, default)
Average O(1) insert, lookup, delete.
Counter counts items. defaultdict(list) groups items.
Keys must be hashable (no lists).

logic.problem: Find two indexes whose values add to a target (unsorted).
logic.thinking: For each number, I only need to know if its partner was seen before.
logic.logic: partner = target - x. Ask the dict instead of searching.
logic.approach:
1. Walk the list.
2. If partner in seen, answer.
3. Else store x.

lessons.title: 10. Comprehensions and Built-ins
lessons.notes:
[x*x for x in a if x > 0]
{k: v for ...} and {x for ...}
zip, map, filter, any, all, sum, min, max, sorted
Generator expression: sum(x for x in a) uses no extra list.

lessons.title: 11. Sorting and Custom Keys
lessons.notes:
sorted(a) returns a new list. a.sort() sorts in place.
key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1])
Sort is stable and O(n log n).
functools.cmp_to_key for custom compare.

lessons.title: 12. Recursion and the Call Stack
lessons.notes:
Every recursion needs a base case and a smaller step.
Python default depth is about 1000. sys.setrecursionlimit(10**6) raises it, but deep recursion can still crash.
Python does not optimise tail calls.

logic.thinking: 2^n is 2^(n/2) squared. The problem halves each time.
logic.approach:
1. Base: n == 0 gives 1.
2. half = f(n // 2).
3. Square it, times x if n is odd.

lessons.title: 13. Classes for DSA
14. Time and Space Complexity in Python
lessons.notes:
list: index O(1), append O(1), insert/pop(0) O(n), x in list O(n)
dict/set: add, lookup, delete O(1) average
deque: both ends O(1)
str: slicing and += cost O(n)
sorted: O(n log n)

logic.thinking: List the operations you do most, then pick the structure where those are cheap.
logic.logic: Lookup: set/dict. Both ends: deque. Order/priority: heap.
logic.approach:
1. Write the operations.
2. Check the cost table.
3. Pick the cheapest fit.
logic.code: # 'x in list' is O(n); 'x in set' is O(1)

lessons.title: 15. collections: deque, Counter, defaultdict
lessons.notes:
from collections import deque, Counter, defaultdict
dq.append, dq.appendleft, dq.pop, dq.popleft
Counter(a).most_common(k)
defaultdict(int) never raises KeyError.

lessons.title: 16. heapq and bisect
lessons.notes:
heapq is a min-heap on a list.
heappush, heappop, heapify, nlargest, nsmallest
Max-heap: push negative values.
bisect_left / bisect_right find positions in a sorted list in O(log n).

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

lessons.title: 17. itertools and functools
18. Two Pointers and Sliding Window
lessons.notes:
Two pointers: sorted data or in-place changes.
Sliding window: a continuous range that grows on the right and shrinks on the left.

logic.problem: Longest substring with no repeated letter.
logic.thinking: Brute force checks every substring. Neighbouring substrings share most letters.
logic.logic: Grow right. If invalid, shrink left until valid again.
logic.approach:
1. Move r, add the letter.
2. While repeated, move l.
3. Track max length.

lessons.title: 19. Linked Lists
lessons.notes:
A node holds a value and a pointer.
Dummy head avoids special cases.
Reverse: keep prev and curr.
Fast and slow pointers find the middle or a cycle.

logic.thinking: Each node must point backwards instead of forwards.
logic.logic: Remember next before you overwrite it.
logic.approach:
1. prev = None.
2. nxt = cur.next.
3. cur.next = prev, then move both.
logic.code:
prev = None
while cur:
    nxt = cur.next
    cur.next = prev
    prev, cur = cur, nxt
return prev

lessons.title: 20. Stacks and Queues
lessons.notes:
Stack: a list with append and pop.
Queue: deque with append and popleft. Never use list.pop(0).
Monotonic stack finds the next greater item.

logic.thinking: The most recent opening bracket must close first.
logic.logic: A closer must match the top of the stack.
logic.approach:
1. Push openers.
2. On a closer, pop and compare.
3. Stack must end empty.

lessons.title: 21. Binary Search
lessons.notes:
Needs sorted or monotonic data. O(log n).
Template: lo, hi, mid = (lo + hi) // 2
Search on answer: binary search over possible results.

logic.problem: Find the smallest speed that finishes in time.
logic.thinking: Bigger speed never hurts, so answers go no, no, yes, yes.
logic.logic: If mid works, try smaller. Else try bigger.
logic.approach:
1. Set lo and hi.
2. Test mid.
3. Shrink the side.
logic.code:
lo, hi = 1, max(piles)
while lo < hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if can_finish(mid): hi = mid
    else: lo = mid + 1
return lo

lessons.title: 22. Trees and Traversals
lessons.notes:
class TreeNode: val, left, right
DFS: preorder, inorder, postorder (recursion)
BFS: level order with deque
Inorder of a BST is sorted.

logic.thinking: A tree's height depends on the heights of its two subtrees.
logic.approach:
1. Empty tree is 0.
2. Ask both children.
3. Take the larger plus 1.
logic.code:
def h(n):
    return 0 if not n else 1 + max(h(n.left), h(n.right))

lessons.title: 23. Graphs: BFS and DFS
lessons.notes:
Adjacency list: g = defaultdict(list)
Use a visited set.
BFS (deque) gives shortest steps in an unweighted graph.
Grid moves: for dx, dy in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)).

logic.thinking: Each island is one connected group of land cells.
logic.logic: Visit a land cell, then sink everything connected to it.
logic.approach:
1. Scan cells.
2. On land, count +1 and flood.
3. Flood marks cells visited.

lessons.title: 24. Shortest Paths and Union Find
lessons.notes:
Dijkstra: heap of (distance, node), for non-negative weights.
Union Find (DSU): find with path compression, union by size.
Use DSU for connected groups and cycle checks.

lessons.title: 25. Backtracking
lessons.notes:
Choose, explore, un-choose.
Save a copy of the path: res.append(path[:]).
Prune early to save time.

logic.problem: List all subsets of a list.
logic.thinking: For each item there are two choices: take it or skip it.
logic.logic: Try a choice, recurse, then undo it.
logic.approach:
1. At index i, add item.
2. Recurse.
3. Remove item, recurse again.
logic.code:
def go(i):
    if i == len(a): res.append(path[:]); return
    path.append(a[i]); go(i + 1)
    path.pop(); go(i + 1)

lessons.title: 26. Dynamic Programming in Python
lessons.notes:
Top-down: @lru_cache(None) on a recursive function.
Bottom-up: fill a list or 2D table.
Space trick: keep only the previous row.
Top 5 to master: Fibonacci, Climbing Stairs, Coin Change, 0/1 Knapsack, LCS.

logic.problem: Minimum coins to make an amount.
logic.thinking: The best answer for amount a uses the best answer for a smaller amount.
logic.pattern: DP: answer built from smaller answers
logic.approach:
1. dp[0] = 0, others infinity.
2. Fill from 1 to amount.
3. Answer is dp[amount] or -1.

lessons.title: 27. Greedy and Intervals
lessons.notes:
Greedy: take the best local choice, and be able to explain why it is safe.
Intervals: sort by start, then merge or count overlaps.

lessons.title: 28. Bit Manipulation and Math
lessons.notes:
& | ^ ~ << >>
x & (x - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
XOR of equal numbers is 0.
pow(a, b, mod), math.gcd, mod 10**9 + 7.

lessons.title: 29. Tries
lessons.notes:
A trie stores words letter by letter.
Node: children = {}, end = False
Insert and search cost O(length of word).

lessons.title: 30. Python Pitfalls and Interview Template
lessons.notes:
Mutable default arguments.
Shallow vs deep copy (copy.deepcopy).
Integer division of negatives floors: -7 // 2 = -4.
Recursion limit.
Template: read input, name the pattern, state complexity, then code.
